validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: this segment is the '广西LNG外输管道复线(百色-文山)工程' ('Guangxi LNG Export Pipeline Duplicate Line, Baise-Wenshan'), a real, actively-tracked national '14th Five-Year' energy project. Confirmed via (1) PipeChina's own 2023-06-07 EIA pre-approval public notice (pipechina.com.cn/front/tzgg/5984.html), signed by 国家管网集团西南管道有限责任公司 = National Pipe Network Group Southwest Pipeline Co Ltd — matches GEM's Operator/Owner exactly — linking to the underlying EIA report PDF (rise.cnpc.com.cn, 22MB); (2) independent construction-launch coverage from Xinhua's Yunnan bureau (yn.xinhuanet.com, 2024-08-09) and PipeChina's own newsroom (pipechina.com.cn/front/news/3001571.html), both dated around the 2024-08-08 groundbreaking, matching GEM's ConstructionYear=2024/ConstructionMonth=8 exactly; (3) a Yunnan Development & Reform Commission construction-start announcement (archived as a screenshot, since the live gov.cn-style page is not stably indexable — visually confirmed the image: '广西LNG外输管道复线（百色－文山）工程开工建设', 2024-08-13, matching GEM's current_ref for Status/ConstructionYear); and (4) a Nov-2025 site-visit report (Yunnan Economic Net / news.jjrbnet.com, 2025-11-12) confirming ongoing construction. Route/location fully confirmed by the EIA PDF: starts 百色首站 (Baise First Station), Youjiang District, Baise City, Guangxi; ends 砚山末站 (Yanshan Terminal Station), Yanshan County, Wenshan Zhuang and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan — exact match to GEM's StartLocation/EndLocation/Province/Country fields. CLASSIFICATION correct: this is a gas transmission line, the 'duplicate/parallel' (复线) branch of the Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline network reaching into Yunnan, tying in at Baise to the West-East Gas Pipeline 2 Nanning-Baise branch and (per the EIA) carrying regasified Beihai LNG plus China-Myanmar pipeline gas onward to Yunnan. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 43-row Guangxi roster: no overlap — P4723 is the only row with an endpoint outside Guangxi (Yunnan/Wenshan/Yanshan County); every other 'Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline' segment (P4715/4716/4718/4719/4720/4721) terminates inside Guangxi with distinct start locations, lengths and diameters — normal multi-segment network tracking, not a relabeled duplicate of P4723.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile LengthKnown: GEM currently records 344.40 km (from the 2022-23 EIA report); every independent post-approval/construction source states 346.8 km. Recommend updating to 346.8 km, or footnoting both with dates.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current_ref for Length (pipechina.com.cn/front/tzgg/5984.html) is itself just a notice/index page that states no figures at all — the actual supporting document is the EIA PDF it links to (rise.cnpc.com.cn/.../c01c27842b7a4a9c85d277c3781801c9.pdf, dated 2023). I downloaded and pdftotext'd that 22MB PDF directly: it states '本工程管道全长约344.4km' / 'DN500：344.4km' repeatedly (18+ occurrences) — an EXACT match to GEM's 344.40 km, alongside DN500 diameter and 10MPa pressure (also exact matches to GEM). HOWEVER every independent source describing the pipeline AFTER it moved from EIA/design stage into approval and construction gives a different figure: PipeChina's own newsroom (2024-08), Xinhua's Yunnan bureau (2024-08-09), the Yunnan DRC's construction-start notice (2024-08-13), and the Nov-2025 Yunnan Economic Net site-visit report all consistently say '全长346.8公里' (346.8 km) — a small (~0.7%) but completely consistent discrepancy across 4 independent, differently-sourced, later-dated documents. Most likely explanation: a minor route/length refinement between the 2022-23 EIA design and the final approved/as-built alignment. Per the 2+ independent corroboration standard, 346.8 km is now the better-supported figure (medium tier from a single EIA doc vs high tier from 4 independent post-approval sources).

validity.recommendation: Verify SegmentCost=2,941,000,000 RMB — the underlying EIA states total investment 2.972 billion RMB (excl. VAT) / construction investment 2.877 billion RMB, and neither matches GEM's figure exactly. Confirm which vintage/basis GEM's number was drawn from (e.g. an intermediate draft), or correct.
validity.researcher_notes: The EIA PDF (rise.cnpc.com.cn, 2023) states '工程总投资29.72×10^8元(不含增值税)，其中环保投资1.37×10^8元' (total investment RMB 2.972bn excl. VAT, of which RMB 137m is environmental) and separately '建设投资28.77×10^8元' (construction investment RMB 2.877bn). GEM's SegmentCost of RMB 2,941,000,000 sits between these two figures but matches neither exactly (~1% off both). Given this project went through at least two EIA submissions (an April-2022 draft, now a dead CNPC link, and this June-2023 resubmission), the 2.941bn figure may come from the earlier draft or a different accounting basis (e.g. incl./excl. a specific cost category) — I could not locate a document stating exactly 2,941,000,000. Flagging rather than silently passing per the corroboration standard; not a large discrepancy (~1%), but real.

validity.recommendation: Clarify FuelSource: consider whether it should describe the physical upstream tie-in (West-East 2 Nanning-Baise branch, currently recorded) vs. the actual gas-of-origin the EIA names (regasified Guangxi/Beihai LNG + China-Myanmar pipeline gas, near-term).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records FuelSource as 'West-East Gas Pipeline 2 Guangzhou-Nanning Branch, Baise branch pipeline(Nanning-Baise)'. The EIA PDF does confirm this as the pipeline's physical origin/interface point ('本工程与上游西气东输二线南宁至百色支线工程的工程界面...'; '广西LNG外输管道复线(百色-文山)工程起自西气东输二线南宁-百色支线'), so the value is textually supported as an INTERCONNECTION description. But the EIA's own gas-source-composition section states something more specific: '本工程近期气源为广西LNG与中缅管道天然气，中远期气源为川渝资源' (near-term gas source = Guangxi LNG [regasified] + China-Myanmar pipeline gas; medium/long-term = Sichuan-Chongqing resources) — and the independent Nov-2025 Yunnan Economic Net piece corroborates this, describing the project as bringing 'surplus Guangxi LNG resources' to Yunnan to form a 'dual gas-source guarantee' alongside the China-Myanmar pipeline. So GEM's current value describes the upstream pipe network tie-in (defensible), while the actual gas being transported is LNG-sourced + Myanmar-pipeline gas, not West-East 2 line-pack per se. Flagging as an attribution nuance to confirm GEM's schema convention (tie-in point vs. gas origin) rather than a clear error.

fills.researcher_notes: This is explicitly a natural-gas pipeline throughout every source consulted (天然气管道; '每年可为滇东南地区输送10亿立方米天然气' — delivers 1 bcm/y of natural gas). Fuel=Gas is unambiguous.

fills.researcher_notes: PipeChina's own 2023-06-07 EIA pre-approval notice for this exact project is signed '国家管网集团西南管道有限责任公司 2023年6月7日' — an exact match to GEM's recorded operator/owner. NOTE: url_verifier's automated content check FAILS on this URL for Chinese-token expected strings — confirmed this is a tool-side encoding bug, not a missing-content issue: the site serves UTF-8 without a charset header, requests.get() defaults to ISO-8859-1, and its .text garbles all non-ASCII content. Numeric/ASCII-only expected tokens (dates, digits) pass fine on this and other Chinese-language URLs in this pilot; only CJK expected-substring checks are affected. I manually re-fetched with r.encoding='utf-8' and confirmed '国家管网集团西南管道有限责任公司' is present verbatim on the page. This likely affects other Chinese-source citations tracker-wide and is worth a one-time engine fix (requests should use r.apparent_encoding, or a charset sniff, before the text/substring check) rather than a per-row workaround — flagging for the orchestrator/engine owner rather than patching scripts/url_verifier.py from inside this fan-out.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched for any post-2024 status update (completion/operating, shelving, cancellation). Newest independent evidence found: Yunnan Economic Net (news.jjrbnet.com), dated 2025-11-12, reporting a PipeChina Yunnan-branch media site visit — construction has been ongoing since 2024-08, comprehensive progress has exceeded 50%, welding mileage has surpassed 263 km, and the project is 'expected to be fully complete and ready for production capability by 2026' (预计2026年全面建成具备投产条件). This directly confirms Status=construction is STILL CORRECT as of Nov 2025 — the line is not yet operating, not shelved, not cancelled. No contradicting or more-recent evidence found. Recommend re-checking again once 2026 arrives, since the same source projects completion within that year.

summary: P4723 (Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline, Baise-Wenshan Branch) is real and correctly classified — confirmed via PipeChina's own EIA filing plus independent Xinhua/PipeChina/Yunnan-government/Yunnan-media coverage, construction ongoing per Nov-2025 evidence (status confirmed, no change); flagged 3 caveats: LengthKnown likely should be 346.8 km not 344.4 km (4 independent post-EIA sources agree on 346.8), SegmentCost doesn't exactly match either EIA investment figure (~1% off), and FuelSource describes the upstream tie-in rather than the EIA's stated gas-source composition (Guangxi LNG + China-Myanmar gas) — plus added refs for Fuel/Operator/Owner (previously MISSING_REF). Also surfaced a tool-side url_verifier encoding bug (ISO-8859-1 vs UTF-8) that produces false-negative content checks on Chinese-language pages tracker-wide.
